abstract: Challenges in natural sciences can often be phrased as optimization problems. Machine learning techniques have recently been applied to solve such problems. One example in chemistry is the design of tailor-made organic materials and molecules, which requires efficient methods to explore the chemical space. We present a genetic algorithm (GA) that is enhanced with a neural network (DNN) based discriminator model to improve the diversity of generated molecules and at the same time steer the GA. We show that our algorithm outperforms other generative models in optimization tasks. We furthermore present a way to increase interpretability of genetic algorithms, which helped us to derive design principles.
claim: Substantially improve the penalized logP of a given molecule while keeping the result chemically similar to it.
interface:
Write one Python module that defines:

  run(spec: dict) -> list[str]

spec = {"start": <SMILES>, "similarity_threshold": <float>, "n_return": <int>,
        "seed": <int>, "time_budget_s": <float>}.

Return up to `n_return` SMILES strings: molecules that score better than `start` under
`a2m_task.score` while staying chemically similar to it. A returned molecule counts only if

    a2m_task.similarity(molecule, start) >= spec["similarity_threshold"]

The runner re-parses, re-scores and re-checks similarity itself, and ignores anything your
code reports. Invalid strings, duplicates and molecules that miss the similarity threshold are
all wasted. Stay inside `time_budget_s` seconds of wall clock and use `seed` for randomness.
notes: Scope: similarity-constrained improvement of penalized logP, the paper's constrained task. The unconstrained version is excluded on purpose: its objective is maximised by degenerate structures such as a long carbon chain, which any method can emit without reasoning. The paper's property-targeted generation and its 250k-molecule reference set are out of scope. The visible system uses the tighter similarity threshold of 0.6 because at 0.4 the constraint is loose enough that blind chain extension passes without any search. Development case, not held out. Paper: http://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11655v4
